answer_text:
Let

\[
P_n=\frac{(2-1)(3-1)(5-1)\cdots(p_n-1)}{2\cdot 3\cdot 5\cdots p_n}.
\]

Since the denominator and numerator run over the same primes, this can be written as

\[
P_n=\prod_{k=1}^n \frac{p_k-1}{p_k}
=\prod_{k=1}^n \left(1-\frac{1}{p_k}\right).
\]

Now take logarithms:

\[
\ln P_n=\sum_{k=1}^n \ln\left(1-\frac{1}{p_k}\right).
\]

For \(0<x<1\), we have \(\ln(1-x)\le -x\). Applying this with \(x=1/p_k\),

\[
\ln P_n \le -\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{1}{p_k}.
\]

It is a classical theorem of Euler that the sum of the reciprocals of the primes diverges:

\[
\sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{1}{p_k}=\infty.
\]

Therefore,

\[
-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{1}{p_k}\to -\infty,
\]

so

\[
\ln P_n \to -\infty.
\]

Hence

\[
P_n = e^{\ln P_n}\to 0.
\]

Thus,

\[
\boxed{0}
\]
